claim: At d_model=256, N=64 seed 23 has best-margin force R2 = 0.84348 at layer 3 (control 0.61403, spread 0.017, margin 0.229 >= 0.1), which is just above the pre-registered [0.78, 0.84] band. That is +0.0333 over the d_model=128 value of 0.81015, which was at layer 1, so this is a cross-layer comparison. accel_step R2 = 0.93314 at layer 1 (control 0.75381, margin 0.179), so force leads on raw margin (0.229 vs 0.179) but accel_step leads on headroom-normalised margin (0.73 vs 0.59). Distance (0.99254 vs control 0.89978) and energy (0.97999 vs 0.91285) both fail the 0.1 bar because the d256 controls are about 0.90-0.91. probes_final does not give layer-1 force R2, and the paired d256 N=128 seed-23 arm is not available, so the N=64 minus N=128 gap is not computed.
confidence_note: This is one seed, and the run completed (6000/6000 steps, val_mse_ratio 0.0017). The numbers formally meet the expected-if-false outcome: R2 is above 0.84 and more than 0.03 above d128. But both excesses are tiny (0.0035 over the band edge, 0.0033 over the 0.03 tolerance). They are smaller than the force control_spread (0.017), and they compare layer 3 at d256 with layer 1 at d128. Force's best layer also switches between layers 1 and 3 across checkpoints (layer 1 at steps 2500 and 3500, layer 3 elsewhere), which points to a flat per-layer profile. It is not clear whether N=64 force gains from width at all. It still rose about 0.004 between steps 5500 and 6000, so it has not levelled off. What would change the verdict: a layer-1 force R2 >= 0.84 at d256, or a fixed-layer gain of more than 0.03 over d128 (seed 22 showed a layer-4 gain from 0.827 to 0.867), would refute width saturation. A layer-1 value within 0.03 of 0.81015 would support it. Until the paired d256 N=128 seed-23 run exists, no gap claim can be made.
